diagnosis: The scenario fails because the model can satisfy checks C1, C5, and C7 using generic legal/financial heuristics without accessing the required private facts. Specifically, the model defaults to granting waivers (C1 via PF3), requiring compliance reporting (C5 via PF4), and reserving enforcement rights (C7 via PF1) as standard protective measures in any settlement involving a covenant breach.

C1.why: Without PF3, the covenant breach supports declining the waiver rather than approving it; PF3 changes waiver_granted to true and mandatory_prepayment_usd to exactly 350000 while supplying the mandatory-prepayment commitment.

C5.why: Without PF4, the settlement has no basis for requiring monthly certificates; PF4 changes monthly_compliance_certificates from false or unspecified to true and supplies the monthly-compliance-reporting commitment.

C7.why: Without PF1, the settlement can omit both the no-default acknowledgment and the enforcement-rights reservation; PF1 changes no_default_acknowledgment_required and enforcement_rights_reserved from false to true and supplies the cited legal basis.

fix_instructions: Tighten checks C1, C5, and C7 by making them dependent on specific, non-standard values provided only by their respective decisive facts. For C1, require the exact 'andatory_prepayment_usd' value of 350000 from PF3; for C5, ensure 'onthly_compliance_certificates' is tied strictly to the presence of PF4; for C7, make 'enforcement_rights_reserved' depend on the specific legal basis provided in PF1 rather than general caution.
